page0.text:
...It's windy.
I suppose part of it is being atop a hill.
The breeze is stronger than below, and the chill that pierces my cheeks has a stronger bite.

page1.text:
"Shirou, have you finished talking?"
"...Yeah. I've been made aware of more than I could ever want.
About the Holy Grail War and Masters, too."
"In that case..."

page2.text:
She leans forward and pierces me with a stare.
...That's only natural.
The decision that I make is her business too.

page3.text:
"...Yeah. I don't know if I'm fit for it, but I decided to fight and be a Master.
I'm sorry that I'm an amateur, but do you still agree to take me on as a Master, Saber?"

page4.text: "There is no need for such an agreement. You are my Master. I have already vowed that I would become your sword."

page5.text:
That moment flitters through my mind.
"...That's right. Yeah, it makes me relieved hearing you say that."
I take a deep breath and face Saber again.

page6.text:
"Shake on it, then. Let's do our best, Saber."
I extend my right hand.
I don't know anything about the relationship between Master and Servant, and what we need to do moving forward.
But at the very least, I want to start out on the right foot.

page7.text:
...
"Saber? Oh, are you against shaking hands?"
"...No, that is not true. I was just startled by the suddenness."

page8.text:
Saber says as she takes my hand in hers.
"I vow once again. As long as you have your Command Spells, I will be your sword."

page9.text:
"Okay. I still don't understand everything, but it's good to have you."
Since Saber is so serious, I nod along.

page10.text:
"...Hm."
...Come to think of it, this is an odd sight.
Under the stars in the winter night...
...I'm shaking hands with a girl I just met and exchanging words like some magical contract.

page11.text:
"Ooh. It looks like I can leave you two at it, huh?"
"...!"
I hastily let go of her hand.
When I turn around, there's Tohsaka and...that knight in the red coat standing there.

page12.text: "Look at you two getting along. You weren't even talking until a moment ago. What a change. What, do you fully trust Saber now?"

page13.text:
"Uh, no, that's not it... Wait, I guess you're right.
I don't know anything about Saber yet, but we're going to work together from now on."

page14.text:
"I see. Then you should be on your guard. Now that you guys are in this war, we won't go easy on you either."
"Hm?"
I tilt my head.
It takes me a second for it to sink in.

page15.text:
"...Hey now. You understand we're enemies now, right?
I brought you here because you weren't my enemy yet.
But now you're a Master, right? Then I think there's only one thing to do now."

page16.text:
"Uh... Hmm?"
Well, that's true, but...
"Why? I don't intend to fight you, Tohsaka."

page17.text:
"...Man, just as I thought. Geez, it was meaningless to bring you here."
Tohsaka drops her shoulders.
"Rin."

page18.text:
"What? We promised that you wouldn't talk until I give the go-ahead, Archer."
"I know, but we'll get nowhere at this rate.
There's no need to find out if our opponent is ready or not. If there's an enemy we can defeat easily, we should attack them without holding back."
"Hey, I know that without you having to tell me."

page19.text:
"If you know, then you should act on it. Or what? Are you going to show him mercy again?
...Hm. It couldn't possibly be that there's some special reason...?"

page20.text:
"O-of course not!"
...It's just, you know, I owe him one. Until I clear that up, I just can't fight him fairly."
"...Hrm, you sure are difficult. Then I'll make myself scarce. Call me again after you've straightened that out."

page21.text:
The red knight, Archer, disappears.
Or rather, I just can't see him anymore.
According to Tohsaka, Servants are spirits.

page22.text:
Saber says that she can't turn into spirit form, but I'm sure she could easily if she was Tohsaka's Servant, since Tohsaka is a functional Master.
...Well, aside from that...

page23.text:
"Hey, Tohsaka. That thing you owe me... Are you talking about what happened earlier?"
"Yeah. No matter what the reason may be, you used a Command Spell to stop Saber. So, it won't be fair unless I hold back a bit to balance things out."

page24.text:
"...Balance, huh? You care about weird things, Tohsaka."
"I know. I know this is just piling on some extra weight. But I can't help it, I hate being in debt to people."
She snorts and turns away.

page25.text:
"But, this is for a limited time. Starting tomorrow, I won't hold back, so you should go ahead and make your plans with Saber."
"...Hm. So, this is only for today?"

page26.text:
"That's right. Well, I am the one who brought you here.
Um, so I'll at least look out for you until you get back into town."
With that, Tohsaka starts walking without looking back at us.

page27.text:
"Let us go, Shirou. As she says, it is not good to stay here."
"..."
I nod to Saber and follow Tohsaka.

page28.text:
The three of us descend the hill.
It might be because Tohsaka took the lead, but we make our way back without any conversation.

page29.text:
There is a simple forked road ahead of us.
One path leads to the main street going towards the front of Shinto station, and the other leads to the big bridge connecting to Miyama.
...
Tohsaka stops in front of the intersection.

page30.text:
"Tohsaka? Aren't you coming? We should head to the bridge if we're going home, right?"
"No. Sorry, but you'll have to head home on your own.
I forgot since I've been so occupied with you, but I had other plans. Now that I'm in Shinto, I'm gonna go look for something while I'm here."

page31.text: "Go look for something...as in other Masters?"

page32.text:
"Yeah. I don't know about you, but I've been waiting for this for a long time. For the seven Masters to appear and the night the Holy Grail War begins.
Wouldn't you say that going straight home is a waste? Since I couldn't beat Saber, I won't feel satisfied unless I can take down another Servant."

page33.text:
...
...There is no hesitation in Tohsaka's eyes.
That made me realize...
Tohsaka is a mage.
Her knowledge and attitude as a mage are set.

page35.text:
"So, we part ways here. I've paid back my debt, and it'll just be a pain if we're in each other's faces. After today we'll become enemies."
Why does she have this part of her that's the opposite of a mage?

page36.text:
Tohsaka didn't explain the rules out of a sense of duty.
She just wanted to be fair, and after figuring out my circumstances, supported me.

page37.text:
So now that the situation is clear, it goes back to how it was before.
As a Master, I will be a target for battle from now on.
"..."
Despite all that, Tohsaka made sure to clear the air first.

page38.text:
For her, everything that happened tonight was unnecessary.
"It'll just be a pain if we're in each other's faces."
If that's how she really feels, she shouldn't have gotten involved to begin with.
But she isn't dumb, so she must've known this is how it would go.
And yet still she helped out, all without thinking about cost or benefit.

page39.text:
...The Tohsaka in front of me is so different from the one I see at school.
Even putting it nicely, she's harsh and cranky. A real sourpuss. And so different from what she normally projects that it makes me want to scream, What's up with the way you act at school!?
Man, she almost seems like a fraud.

page40.text:
...Yet, still...
Tohsaka Rin is also exactly how everyone thought she was.

page41.text:
"Yeah. Tohsaka, you're a good person."
"Huh? What's with you? I won't go easy on you even if you try flattery."

page42.text:
I know that.
Because she won't go easy on me, it'll be a pain to also be on the lookout for me. That's what she's saying.

page43.text:
"I know. But if possible, I don't want to be enemies. I like people like you."
"Wha—"

page44.text:
For some reason, Tohsaka falls silent.
These deserted suburbs...
The church that looms in the distance and the stillness of the foreigner cemetery that spreads over the hill feel strangely warm now.

page45.text: "A-anyway, if your Servant gets killed, just run to that church. If you do that, at least your life will be spared."

page46.text:
"Got it. I don't exactly like the idea, but I'll keep it in mind. Highly doubt it'll happen, though. No matter how I look at it, I'll die before Saber does."
"...Ugh."
Tohsaka reacts strangely again.
She lets out a deep sigh as if she's fed up with me and glances at Saber.

page47.text:
"All right, I won't give you any more warnings since then I'll really be going out of my way.
Just be careful. Even with Saber as strong as she is, it won't matter if you, the Master, gets killed."
Tohsaka turns around and starts walking towards Shinto.

page48.text:
However...
She stops dead in her tracks, as if she saw a ghost.

page50.text:
A youthful voice echoes through the night.
The singsong voice is unmistakably that of a young girl.
My line of sight focuses on the top of the hill.
There...

page51.text:
I don't know when the skies cleared, but the moon shines brightly in the night.
The shadow is long and monstrous, like a demon in a picture book.
Amidst the silhouette of the townscape, through the late night gloom, something terrible stands.

page52.text:
"...Berserker."
Tohsaka mumbles a word that I'm not familiar with.
Even if I don't know what that means, I can tell that the giant is something different altogether.

page53.text:
That thing isn't human.
Then... It's one of the beings called Servants, just like Saber and the others.
"Good evening, big brother. This is the second time we've met like this."
The girl says, smiling.
The innocence sends a chill down my spine.
The dissonance between her and that monstrous shape behind her makes me feel like I'm living a nightmare.
...
What I said earlier about a chill down my spine is underselling it.
The chill reaches every part of me, deep into my consciousness.
That thing is a monster.
I'm not even looking directly at it but its very presence is making it hard to move...

page54.text:
"...I'm surprised. If we're talking just raw power, that thing surpasses Saber."
She clicks her tongue and glares at the monster above us.
From her back alone, I can tell she is just as terrified as I am, but also determined not to lose to that thing.

page55.text:
"Archer, that thing isn't something that can be fought head-on. Fight it with your class specialty."
Her voice is barely more than a whisper.
The unmaterialized knight gives his response.

page56.text:
"Understood. But what about your defense? You cannot avoid a charge."
"There's three of us. If it's just playing defense, we can manage."
He must have nodded to that.
The presence hanging around Tohsaka vanishes instantly.

page57.text:
"Emiya. It's up to you whether you want to run or fight.
...But, if you can, I'd say make a break for it."

page58.text:
"Are you done with your little strategy session? Can I start now?"
A playful laugh.
The girl gives a polite bow, incongruous to this entire situation.

page59.text:
"Nice to meet you, Rin. I'm Illya.
Illyasviel von Einzbern...you know what that means, right?"
"Einzbern—"
She seems familiar with the name and wavers in place.

page60.text:
The girl smiles happily in response to Tohsaka's reaction, and says,
"I'll kill you now. Get her, Berserker."
She croons to the monster behind her.
